title: Canonical direct-image limit comparison as a morphism of Roos triangles
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with a specified ring isomorphism $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Module pullback $F=f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to module direct image $G=f_*$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ringed-topos convention [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$.
Assume countable products of module sheaves on both sites are exact. Use $\mathcal G=Rf_*$, $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}=Rf_*^{\rm Tow}$ and the normalized comparison $a_M:\mathcal G R\lim_X M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_Y\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. For a derived strict tower $M$, the product comparison
$$\alpha_M:\mathcal G\bigl(\prod_n^D M_n\bigr)\longrightarrow\prod_n^D(\mathcal GM_n)$$
with components $\mathcal G(p_n)$ is invertible and commutes with transition endomorphisms, hence with $1-s$. The triple $(a_M,\alpha_M,\alpha_M)$ is a morphism from $\mathcal G$ of the canonical Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] of $M$ to the canonical Roos triangle of $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$, including the connecting square with the canonical shift comparison. Here $R\lim$ is total right derived inverse limit of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and the canonical Roos triangle of a derived strict tower $N$ is fixed as follows. For a complex $X$ of strict towers representing $N$, let $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ be the strict Roos model of [def-weil-strict-roos-model], with coordinates $(y,x)\in\prod_nX_n^{r-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^r$. Take its rotated cone triangle $H(X)\xrightarrow{r}\prod_nX_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nX_n\xrightarrow{b}H(X)[1]$, where $r(y,x)=x$ and $b(z)=(z,0)$, with termwise products representing $\prod^D$. Transport it to $R\lim N$ along the isomorphism $Q(H(X))\cong R\lim N$. That isomorphism is the unit-normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-products-roos-comparison], composed with the chain isomorphism $(y,x)\mapsto(-y,x)$ from the fibre of $-(1-s)$ to $H(X)$. On a K-injective $X$ this is transport along the ordinary-limit inclusion with coordinates $(0,(\lambda_n)_n)$. The canonical shift comparison $\sigma$ of $\mathcal G$ is the one compatible with the derived-functor units of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]: $\sigma_{QK}\circ\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]$ for every complex $K$. The first component is precisely the underived-composite normalized $a_M$, rather than an unspecified cone isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-adjoint-tower-models] to $F\dashv G$. Represent $M$ by an injective-term K-injective tower $I$ and put $J=G^{\rm Tow}I$. Use its notation $L_I,L_J,P_I,P_J,c,\beta$. That lemma identifies $Q(c)$ with $\alpha_M$, proves it invertible, and gives both the $s$ and $1-s$ squares; all derived composites are computed on these same models.

proof.text: Put $u_I=1-s_I$, $u_J=1-s_J$ and $H_T=\operatorname{Cone}(u_T)[-1]$ for $T=I,J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-fiber-triangle-comparison] with $P_I,P_J,c$: its hypotheses hold by Step 1, and $G$ preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. It gives the K-injective cones, diagonal chain isomorphism $\theta:G(H_I)\cong H_J$, all three cone-triangle squares and the unique shift $\sigma$ with the stated unit normalization.

proof.text: By the exact-products clause of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-adjoint-tower-models], the inclusions $j_T:L_T\to H_T$, $z\mapsto(0,(\lambda_nz)_n)$, for $T=I,J$ are quasi-isomorphisms, and $\kappa_TQ(j_T)=\eta^{\lim}_T$ for precisely the sign-corrected, unit-normalized comparison in the statement. Thus the canonical Roos triangles are Step 2's cone triangles transported along $Q(j_I),Q(j_J)$.

proof.text: The diagonal coordinates and $\lambda_n\beta=G(\lambda_n)$ give the chain equality $\theta G(j_I)=j_J\beta$: both first coordinates are zero, and every second-coordinate leg is $G(\lambda_n)$. Both derived composites are computed on $I$ without another resolution (Step 1). Hence the common-underived-composite normalization in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] identifies $a_M=Q(\beta)$. Conjugating gives $Q(j_J)^{-1}Q(\theta)\mathcal G(Q(j_I))=a_M$. Transport Step 2's three squares along these inclusions. The components are $(a_M,\alpha_M,\alpha_M)$, and the last square is $a_M[1]\sigma_{R\lim_X M}\mathcal G(\delta_M)=\delta_{\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M}\alpha_M$. Naturality and localization extend the equations from the K-injective models to all derived strict towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived].
